title: Total mass is 0 or ∞ for a measure on ℝ^P with Euclidean lower density bounds at its support points
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n. Let μ be a measure on (the Borel σ-algebra of) ℝ^P = Euclid P, and let ω_n := unitBallVolume n, the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n. Assume: every w ∈ ℝ^P with μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 satisfies ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ μ(B_ρ(w)) for every ρ > 0. Here B denotes the open ball and ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal. Then μ(ℝ^P) = 0 or μ(ℝ^P) = ∞.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), 1 ≤ n → (∀ w : Euclid P, (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → μ (ball w ε) ≠ 0) → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) ≤ μ (ball w ρ)) → μ univ = 0 ∨ μ univ = ∞
